_comment: DRISHTI AppSail deploy descriptor (Phase 14 Part D / matrix rows 2,3). NOT the CLI app-config.json: Catalyst custom OCI (Docker) runtimes do NOT use app-config.json - config is supplied via `catalyst deploy appsail` flags and the Console. This file is the single reviewed source of those intended values, consumed by the CI/CD pipeline and the runbook. No secret VALUES are stored here - only the KEYS that must be set server-side in the Console/AppSail configuration.

instance_correctness.why: Prompt 21 §G.1 — for hackathon simplicity AppSail is pinned to exactly ONE instance (min=max=1) so in-process ID allocation (disaster/board next_id seeded from max) and the signed-context nonce replay guard are correct without distributed coordination. Proven by this max=1 setting + the deploy command's single-instance scale.
instance_correctness.shared_state_defence_in_depth: In addition to the single-instance pin, the signed-context nonce replay guard also records nonces in Catalyst Cache (segment 'nonce') via atomic set-if-absent when DRISHTI_USE_CATALYST_CACHE=true, so replay is caught across instances should the cap ever be raised (app/gateway_context.py _nonce_is_replay).
instance_correctness.backlog: Multi-instance (max>1) requires shared monotonic ID allocation (Catalyst Data Store sequence / Cache incr) for disaster/board PKs and is tracked in the backlog; do NOT raise instances.max above 1 until that lands.

notes: catalyst_auth=false: DRISHTI uses its own gateway facade + signed context; the Catalyst SSO wrapper would break that flow.

instances pinned to min=max=1 (Prompt 21 §G.1 instance correctness): single-instance makes in-process ID allocation + nonce replay correct without distributed coordination, and also controls hackathon credit. See instance_correctness above before raising max.

Public access is via the API Gateway -> gateway_api function -> AppSail. With DRISHTI_REQUIRE_GATEWAY_CONTEXT=true the app ACTIVELY REJECTS (401) any non-health request that lacks a valid signed context, so direct unauthenticated browser CRUD against the AppSail URL is refused (items 10/12).
The image excludes torch/CUDA/TabFM/TabPFN/TimesFM/torch-geometric; model compute is on external AWS GPU (services/gpu-worker).

Build + deploy via infra/catalyst/appsail/deploy.ps1 (CLI-driven; `catalyst deploy appsail --name --source --port` — note: CLI 1.27.0 has NO 'standalone' subcommand). Deploy is credit-spending and opt-in (-Deploy).

key_notes.DRISHTI_REQUIRE_GATEWAY_CONTEXT: true in deployment: AppSail verifies the signed gateway/service context (signature/audience/scope/expiry/replay) before handling any non-health request and rejects unauthenticated browser CRUD (items 10/12). Unset/false locally.
key_notes.DRISHTI_CONTEXT_AUDIENCE: Expected audience the signed context is minted for; must equal the value embedded by the Node signers (default 'drishti-appsail'). Empty string disables the audience check.
key_notes.DRISHTI_USE_CATALYST_STRATUS: true so evidence/import/report objects use Catalyst Stratus (not the in-memory fake).
key_notes.DRISHTI_ACCESS_LOG_ENABLED: true to emit structured, redacted JSON access logs (method/path/status/latency/request_id/role/scope) to stdout.
key_notes.DRISHTI_AWS_ADAPTER_CB_FAILURES: Part F item 5: consecutive AWS-adapter failures that trip the client circuit breaker (default 5).
key_notes.DRISHTI_AWS_ADAPTER_CB_RESET_S: Part F item 5: circuit-breaker cooldown seconds before a half-open probe (default 30).
key_notes.DRISHTI_STREAM_CHANNEL_ENABLED: Part F item 1: true to enable the scoped direct-AppSail SSE channel (/stream/predictions). OFF => the endpoint returns 404 (no surface).
key_notes.DRISHTI_CHANNEL_SIGNING_SECRET: HMAC secret for the scoped channel token; falls back to ZOHO_APPSAIL_SIGNING_SECRET. Must match the channel_token function's secret.
key_notes.DRISHTI_CHANNEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: Comma-separated EXACT browser origins allowed to open the channel (strict Origin check). Required when the channel is enabled.
key_notes.DRISHTI_APPSAIL_STREAM_URL: Set on the channel_token FUNCTION (not AppSail): https base URL of the AppSail SSE endpoint returned to the browser.
key_notes.DRISHTI_CHANNEL_TTL_MS: Channel-token lifetime in ms (default 300000 = 5 min); the stream self-closes at expiry, forcing a re-handshake through the gateway.
key_notes.DRISHTI_AWS_ADAPTER_URL: Required HTTPS API Gateway base URL for Bedrock and retained AWS model operations.
key_notes.DRISHTI_AWS_ADAPTER_SECRET: Required shared HMAC secret, configured only in AppSail and AWS Secrets Manager; never commit or expose it to the browser.
key_notes.SEMANTIC_PLANNER_PROVIDER: Set to aws_bedrock. AppSail prefers the existing signed AWS adapter and may use explicit direct SDK failover with the dedicated least-privilege IAM user.
key_notes.BEDROCK_MODEL_ID: Must be exactly zai.glm-4.7-flash. Code and AWS IAM both reject Claude, GPT/OpenAI, and any unreviewed model.
key_notes.BEDROCK_REGION: Set to us-east-1 for the current GLM 4.7 Flash Bedrock endpoint.
key_notes.BEDROCK_DIRECT_SDK_ENABLED: Optional local/profile opt-in. In AppSail, the dedicated least-privilege AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY server-side variables enable direct failover even when this flag is false or blank.

env_var_keys.database_url_policy: Prompt 23 Option A (hackathon deviation, documented): DATABASE_URL IS now set on the AppSail so it accesses the synthetic AWS RDS (drishti-db, ap-south-1) SERVER-TO-SERVER for the operational CRUD domains still on RDS (intake/cases/casework/evidence/chat/governance/etc. - deployment_boundary.py migration=rds_backed_migration_pending). The BROWSER never reaches RDS (browser -> API Gateway -> gateway_api -> signed context -> AppSail -> RDS). Chosen for live-demo completeness instead of the full Data Store migration. Bounded because: the DB is synthetic (verify_hackathon_startup enforces the synthetic_meta.app_environment marker at boot and refuses a non-synthetic DB), RLS is off by explicit hackathon request, and Board/Disaster remain Data Store-native. Revert by removing DATABASE_URL to fall back to Data-Store-only operational serving.
